what_it_does: Intel's Clearwater Forest is the next generation Xeon processor (Intel's line of server chips for datacenters). It improves power efficiency—meaning it uses less electricity to do the same amount of work—by mixing two kinds of cores: powerful performance cores that handle demanding tasks and lightweight efficiency cores for lighter-weight work. This allows the chip to flexibly shift which type of core handles each task, letting the processor balance speed versus power consumption based on what workloads are running.
